validation_environment: Host reader/Java tests on macOS; full transactions in disposable Debian 12 aarch64/Python 3.11/ksh93 container without network; native and real firmware shell checks on QNX/QEMU. Mounts mocked.
limits: No vehicle result for this package, including Android Auto on MU1367.
Safe area: whether the taller v1.2.2 area brings back a closer, lighter map and how much of the route sits under the dials is a car result; frame sizes depend on the phone app.
Backlog limit 2048: absorbs bursts up to about 250 ms of video before a reset; a real stall shows up to about 250 ms of older video before the reset (was about 125 ms).

CarPlay bridge reclaim: the cause (factory encoder taking isoTX2 at boot) is read from one full boot log and matches three exports; the reclaim itself is tested off-unit with a simulated ENOMEM and a fake dmdt. The rebuilt bridge (clang with the pinned QNX 6.5 SDK binutils) replaces the upstream GCC 4.9.4 build, which cannot be reproduced locally.

Android Auto: the hook binary is the pinned upstream build (car-tested on MU1161); the v1.5.0-e feeder and hook were tried in one MU1367 car (map froze, guidance worked); the v1.5.1-e bridge build is tested off-unit only.
The freeze diagnosis rests on code and a host reproduction; the car export lacked the AA bridge counters.
Android Auto: no first-step arrow, no remaining distance/time, lanes or road name; 30 fps; a lost picture returns only after the phone reconnects.
An OEM reset run outside the menu leaves the gal wrapper in place (it then runs the factory gal); the saved Android Auto controller restores the file.
Driving-side U-turn lanes are tested off-unit only; no left-hand-traffic capture exists.
The Apple Maps name merge covers names containing the word Apple; flip timing within a route is not captured.
Whether 25 fps reduces stutter is untested; the delivered frame rate may fall with the request.
Stream values 5 and 6 (20 and 27 fps) are unknown to v1.4.5 and older menus.
The 3-minute quiet hold can show a last maneuver for at most that time if an app stops without a route-end state.
Physical remount/storage and power-loss durability are not established.
